evals.prompt: Add an "Add member" flow to the team settings page. It should open a right-side drawer with name, email, role select and an optional note. Required fields must validate, a failed save shows an error banner, and everything is disabled while saving.
evals.expected_output: A feature drawer that composes the pre-built DrawerRoot with a form body, field-level errors, a destructive error banner, a footer with Cancel and a Save button that shows a Loader2 spinner and disables the form while submitting.
assertions: Imports DrawerRoot from ~/components/shared/DrawerRoot.vue and never rebuilds the drawer shell
Save button renders Loader2 with animate-spin while saving and the fields are disabled
The submit-failure banner uses bg-destructive/10 text-destructive, not bg-muted
Field errors render below the input in text-destructive with an AlertCircle icon
Inputs use the focus-visible:ring-ring focus treatment

evals.prompt: We need a simple login form on the auth page — just email and password with a show/hide toggle and a submit button that shows a spinner. Two fields only, keep it on the page.
evals.expected_output: An inline form (no drawer) with email and password fields, an Eye/EyeOff password visibility toggle, and a submit button with loading and disabled states.
assertions: Uses the inline form pattern, not a drawer
Password visibility toggles between Eye and EyeOff icons
The submit button shows a Loader2 spinner and is disabled while loading
Submit button keeps the tactile hover:scale-[1.02] active:scale-[0.98] classes

evals.prompt: In the settings panel, add a tiny inline form to rename the current workspace (single text field, max 40 chars) with Save and Cancel.
evals.expected_output: A one-field inline form with validation for the 40-character limit, disabled Save while submitting, and the shared input/button token styles.
assertions: Uses the inline pattern for the single-field case
Validates the 40-character limit and shows a field error when exceeded
Save shows the loading state and disables while in flight
Input and button styling uses design tokens (border-input, ring-ring, bg-primary) with no hardcoded colours
